records.title: Coinbase Global Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — lending, derivatives and customer collateral
records.note: As of 2026-09-30, Coinbase reports $1.2995B crypto assets held as collateral, $389.657M crypto assets borrowed and $1.976B loan receivables. Recognized lending collateral totals $1.009297B including $997.557M crypto and $11.740M fiat/payment stablecoins; crypto breakdown BTC $920.649M, ETH $67.005M, other crypto $9.903M. Recognized derivatives collateral is $301.943M (BTC $298.212M, ETH $3.731M); derivatives collateral requirements are at least 100% of notional. Loan collateral requirements range 100%-250% of loan fair value. Separate customer collateral not recognized as an asset or obligation to return totals $3.284562B ($2.804112B crypto, $480.450M fiat/payment stablecoins). No XRP amount is named; derivatives table lists only BTC/ETH. Over nine months, customer crypto collateral received was $3.038805B and returned $2.731034B; crypto loan receivables originated $3.562896B and repaid $3.562928B. These are gross flows, not XRP flows.

records.title: Visa Onchain Analytics — stablecoin transactions and adjusted-volume methodology
records.note: Visa's dashboard explains that raw onchain stablecoin activity includes bots and other programmatic transactions that may not represent settlement; its adjusted methodology filters inorganic activity and uses Allium data. The current static page displays more than $272B global circulating stablecoin supply and $10.2T adjusted global transaction volume over the last 12 months. Dashboard values are dynamic; preserve retrieval time and methodology version.

records.title: Cointelegraph — Stablecoin volume hits record $1.79T in June, Visa says
records.note: Reports Visa/Allium adjusted stablecoin volume of $1.79T in June 2026; USDC approximately $1.21T or 67% of June adjusted volume; USDT approximately 32%; H1 adjusted stablecoin volume $8.82T and USDC about 70% of H1 adjusted volume. Secondary report; the primary Visa dashboard documents the adjustment methodology. Not directly comparable with Circle's company-reported $36T H1 onchain volume and 77% June share without harmonized definitions.

records.title: Binance Security Incident Update — 2026-10-30 02:23 UTC
records.note: Binance's initial investigation suggests a compromised DevOps engineer laptop allowed access to a service container and unauthorized withdrawals; Binance says it found no evidence of wallet private-key leakage. Binance estimates total impact around $6.3B, says approximately $3B was frozen onchain, deposits/withdrawals were temporarily suspended, affected address authorization revoked, and it will cover losses from SAFU and company funds. It plans an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation. These are company statements and preliminary estimates, not an independent post-mortem.

records.title: CoinDesk — Binance hack drained wallets backing customer assets, reserve data shows
records.note: CoinDesk reports its review of Binance's October 1 PoR found the Ethereum wallet labelled Binance 14 among published reserve addresses; at that snapshot it held approximately 89,475 ETH and 1.26B USDT. The article estimates ETH reserve coverage may have fallen below 100% after approximately 204,500 ETH was taken. This is about the Binance 14 EVM wallet and does not identify or cross-reference the five Binance-labelled XRPL source wallets in the separate 233.46M XRP transfer.

records.title: Binance Proof of Reserves — official methodology and address download page
records.note: Binance describes its PoR as user-custody asset coverage using address-ownership verification, point-in-time customer-balance snapshots, Merkle trees and zk-SNARK proofs. The page exposes a dynamic Download All Address control but the static web extraction in this run did not expose the underlying downloadable file. No direct crosswalk of the five XRPL source wallets against the October 1 XRP reserve address set was completed.
